item.title: Justin Cary, Sixpence None the Richer Bassist, Dies at 50
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we share the latest news and updates from the music world. Today, we're sad to report the passing of Justin Cary, the longtime bassist for Sixpence None the Richer. He was just 50 years old.
[Soft music continues in the background]
Host: According to the band's singer, Leigh Nash, and a GoFundMe campaign, Cary passed away on Thursday, June 18th, after recently suffering a stroke. Nash took to Instagram to pay tribute to her bandmate, saying "We sure had a great time" was an understatement, and that Justin was a one-of-a-kind person.
[Pause for a moment]
Host: Cary had been receiving treatment at Albany Medical Center in New York after suffering a serious stroke. The GoFundMe page, which was set up to support Cary and his wife Linda, stated that he passed peacefully, with Linda by his side.
[Soft music continues]
Host: As a member of Sixpence None the Richer, Cary played a key role in the band's success, including the hit song "Kiss Me", which peaked at number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100. He joined the band in 1997 and went on to play with other notable artists, such as Counting Crows, Jennifer Knapp, and Lee Brice.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: Our thoughts are with Justin's family, friends, and bandmates during this difficult time. We'll miss his contribution to the music world, but his legacy will live on through the music he created. Thanks for tuning in to this special report. We'll be back with more news and updates soon.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
